queries.text: Which four hypotheses, each uniform in the volume, the background field, the regulator and the real energy, on the weighted coefficients of the slow (retained, low) block - a cubic remainder, a quadratic remainder on the off-diagonal coupling vector, a first-order size bound and a strict contraction of the fast-block perturbation - are needed before the Schur complement excess is bounded to third order?

In the Feshbach / Schrieffer-Wolff block reduction of a coupled operator, what four operator inequalities on the weighted retained-space coefficients (cubic remainder, quadratic remainder on the coupling vector, first-order norm bound, strict contraction of the perturbation of the high block) must hold uniformly in volume, background field, regulator and real energy so that the excess of the reduced quadratic form (effective potential) is controlled to third order?

Hypotheses for a third-order Schur excess bound: cubic remainder on the retained-space coefficients, quadratic remainder on the coupling vector, first-order size bound, strict contraction of the fast-block perturbation, all uniform with respect to volume, background field, regulator and real energy.

Uniform-in-volume Schur complement bound: which four weighted-coefficient inequalities on the slow block and the coupling to the hard block, uniform in background, regulator and energy, precede the cubic error bound on the reduced form?
